workflow: Manually reviewing and processing flags in the moderator queue, especially for spam, low-quality, and duplicate posts
trigger: User reports a post via flagging interface
current_workaround: Moderators work through the queue manually, often using browser extensions or custom scripts to speed up bulk actions like deleting multiple spam posts
consequence: Backlog of flags builds up, spam stays visible longer, low-quality content reduces site quality, moderator burnout

workflow: Tracking reputation changes over time across multiple sites, manually recording daily or weekly reputation points because the built-in reputation history is not easily exportable
trigger: Desire to monitor rep growth, identify vote patterns, or prepare for nomination applications
current_workaround: Users copy-paste data from the reputation tab into spreadsheets or use third-party scripts (e.g., Stack Exchange Data Explorer queries) to pull history
consequence: Time wasted on manual data entry, errors in manual transcription, difficulty comparing sites, inability to get historical trends without custom code

workflow: Generating weekly community health reports (questions, answers, votes, flags, users) by manually querying the Stack Exchange Data Explorer (SEDE) and compiling results in a spreadsheet
trigger: Weekly cycle or special review requests from Stack Exchange Inc.
current_workaround: Run SQL queries on SEDE, export CSV, then manually combine and format in Excel/Google Sheets; sometimes automated with scripts but still fragile
consequence: Inconsistent reporting, time sink (hours per week), error-prone, difficult to reproduce or share without manual steps

target_role: Stack Exchange moderator and community manager
workflow: Manually checking for plagiarism and copyright violations in posts, comparing text against original sources, and following up with takedown notices
trigger: User flags a post as plagiarized, or automated detection (e.g., Turnitin) raises a match
current_workaround: Moderators use external search engines, manual comparison, and sometimes custom scripts to check similarity; DMCA takedowns are handled via email with Stack Exchange legal team
consequence: Copyright infringement goes undetected, legal risk, community trust erosion, moderator time diverted from other tasks
